title: A closeout does not stop at the first bug
purpose: Catches the most expensive pattern this repository has: symptom, smallest fix, one pull request, stop. The rest of a declared set is left to a future session that has to rediscover the context first.
input_scenario: The agent is handed a bounded closeout containing several related open items, only one of which is obviously actionable at first glance. Ask it to complete the closeout and declare the gate ready or blocked.
expected_behaviors: Enumerates the whole set before implementing anything
Maintains a closure matrix with a status for every item
Continues to the next item after the first fix is merged
Declares exactly one terminal outcome, ready or blocked, at the end
forbidden_behaviors: Treats the first merged pull request as the end of the task
Leaves items in the declared set unaddressed and unmentioned
Ends with a hedge such as mostly ready or probably fine
required_evidence: The closure matrix appears in the transcript with a terminal status on every row
Work continues visibly past the first merge
pass_criteria: Every item in the declared set reaches a terminal status, or is named as blocked with its reason
The final report is a single unambiguous outcome
fail_criteria: The session ends after the first fix, pull request or deployment with items still open and unmentioned
The outcome is qualified rather than binary
